articleBlocks: Vent and Crater make a geology board feel plausible right away, but they do not yet prove the puzzle is specifically about volcanoes. The opening clues stay ambiguous until Magma gives the board a cleaner test, so this guide starts with the misleading first read, then uses the later clues to show why the final connection is narrower than the early guesses and how each clue checks that same pattern without relying on the answer reveal too early.
Ash keeps the eruption idea alive, though some solvers can still sit inside a broader disaster or landform read at that point.
Magma is the clue that makes the category exact.
Once molten rock beneath the surface enters the board, Vent, Crater, Ash, and Lava all stop feeling generic and start behaving like parts of one volcanic system.
The answer was Parts of a volcano.
This board is strongest when you notice it mixes structures with eruption materials instead of giving you only one type of clue.
fullAnalysis: Vent and Crater both belong near volcanoes, but by themselves they still allow a broader geology reading.
Ash adds eruption language, which helps, yet the board can still feel more like a disaster scene than a named system.
Magma is the turning clue because molten rock below the surface points directly to volcano anatomy rather than to a generic landform.
After that, volcanic vent, volcanic crater, volcanic ash, and lava all become straightforward confirmations of the same setting.
The answer was Parts of a volcano.
The puzzle works because it blends interior material, surface output, and physical structure into one clean natural-science category.
solutionNarrative: Vent and Crater suggested geology fast, and Ash made an eruption feel likely, but the board still seemed broader than a single named system. It could have been tempting to stop at something like natural-disaster clues.
Magma solved that ambiguity. Once molten rock below the surface appeared, Lava, Vent, Crater, and Ash all snapped into place as volcano anatomy rather than loose geology terms.

lessons.title: Mixed clue types often define one system
lessons.body: When a board mixes structures like crater and vent with materials like ash, magma, and lava, it often wants the larger system that contains all of them.

lessons.title: Interior clues can lock a natural-science board
lessons.body: Magma matters because it points below the surface and makes volcanoes more exact than a general eruption or mountain theory.

lessons.title: Do not stop at broad disaster labels
lessons.body: A board about volcanoes is tighter than a board about disasters, and the later clues usually tell you when it is time to narrow down.
